metadata.name: The Connecticut Light and Power Company d/b/a Eversource Energy (CL&P)
metadata.dollar_basis: Nominal dollars. Cumulative figures undiscounted unless labelled npv3_2026 (NPV at 3%, 2026 dollars). Bills are the average residential bill, $/month.
metadata.flows_note: Customer savings split residential / business by the residential share of sales (EIA-861, 2024).
metadata.share_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run at utility_share 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 with every other input fixed (default 0.30). Value creation is held constant across shares: the share moves value between customers and the utility; it does not change what flexibility delivers.
metadata.objective_sweep_note: Each scenario and pace re-run with an additional savings objective of 0 / 2.5 / 5 / 10% of its base (default 0%, base dist_revenue_requirement, net of 20% cost to achieve), every other input fixed. The objective is additional to the other layers by assumption.
metadata.objective_sweep_run_note: Each objective_sweep level carries its full chart data under run (yearly, waterfall_usd_month, value_flows_m), built exactly as the top-level run block.
metadata.earnings_note: earnings_total_m = equity return on rate base + shared savings earnings; earnings_per_rate_base = earnings_total_m / rate base (wires + program regulatory asset).
metadata.advance_note: advance: each scenario with the customer dividend advance on (default off in the model), at its enabled defaults: level bill credit for advance_credit_years from 2027 sized at 0.5 x the PV (at the financing rate) of the Cautious scenario recoverable savings, securitized at 4%, recovered through a rider withholding a share of each year total customer saving vs BAU (bill_savings), on a schedule that tracks credits actually paid; true-up pauses credits when behind schedule; recoveries capped so customers net saving is never negative. advance_stress: sized on Central, realized Cautious. worst_year_vs_bau = the largest shared-savings minus BAU average residential bill.
metadata.fast_start_note: fast_start: each scenario and pace with mechanism.fast_start on (first savings year 2027; near-term ramps at their defaults, i.e. none): yearly, waterfall_usd_month, value_flows_m and headline. advance_fast_start: the advance at its enabled defaults with fast start on; advance_fast_start_stress: the same, sized on Central and realized Cautious.
metadata.allocation_sweep_note: allocation_sweep: each scenario and pace with the pool's customer share (the wires and program revenue-requirement reduction net of shared savings earnings, recovered through delivery rates) split between residential and non-residential customers by_sales (default: residential share of sales, EIA-861), per_customer (equal per customer: residential share of EIA-861 2024 customer counts) or custom (residential share 0.5). Capacity, transmission, losses, wholesale and efficiency energy savings follow load through existing rates and stay split by sales. Totals are the same under every option; by_sales equals the run block. Residential bills move by the reallocated amount per residential customer; non-residential savings per customer use EIA-861 2024 counts, held constant.
metadata.lookback_note: lookback: the starting point 2021-2026 from utilities/<utility>_lookback.json (engine/lookback.py; every figure with source, as_of and status). bill_trend: headline like-for-like trend, EIA-861 2021-2025 at the benchmark usage (delivery and supply where EIA reports delivery-only customers); bill_2026_tariff: the 2026 starting bill by category, shown separately; bill_levels_by_basis: 2021 (EIA) and 2026 (tariff) levels, different bases, not a change. rr_bridge: distribution revenue requirement on a FERC Form 1 functional basis 2021 -> 2025, then the approved 2026 rate-case step ($M nominal); rows (detailed) and grouped_rows (capital-driven, cost of capital, operating with normalised O&M, pension non-service, rate-case step). riders (Dominion): every Virginia rider, residential $/month at 1,000 kWh and revenue requirement by rate year, with the bill bridge. asked_granted_totals: requested against approved, cumulative and %, temporary rates separate. supply_side: influenced, not controlled, by the distribution utility.
metadata.transmission_note: Transmission (split formulation, METHODOLOGY 3.8a): customer savings, value flows and bills count (b), transmission upgrades deferred. (a), the lower share of zonal transmission costs (PJM: a lower network service peak load shifts part of the fixed zonal transmission cost to other customers in the zone), is reported separately as lower_share_of_zonal_transmission_costs (yearly $M and headline $B, undiscounted nominal) with cost_shifted_to_other_zone_customers alongside; it is not in customer savings, bills, the shared-savings pool or shared savings earnings (transmission.allocation_in_headline off). 0 in New York. Connecticut (ISO-NE): the zone is New England. Regional Network Service pools all transmission owners' revenue requirements by 12-coincident-peak network load, so (a) is a cost shift to other New England customers; it is measured on the annual peak and so overstated.
metadata.tornado_note: Tornado at Central (every input at central; low and high one at a time), per pace; change in the average residential monthly saving vs Central.

lookback.note: Look-back module (engine/lookback.py): the starting point 2021-2026. Every figure carries a source, an as_of date and a status (sourced / derived / _VERIFY / setting). The forward model does not read this file. Dollar figures are nominal and undiscounted. Revised 2 Nov 2026: grouped bridge inputs (property tax attribution, O&M normalisation), Dominion riders, like-for-like EIA bill trend, asked-against-granted comparisons, class allocation from the joint proposals and MD PSC orders.

bill_trend.basis: Headline like-for-like trend: EIA-861 residential average revenue per kWh, 2021-2025, x the benchmark usage; delivery = delivery-only (Part C) revenue per kWh x benchmark, supply = bundled - delivery. The 2026 tariff bill is shown separately; 2021 EIA averages and the 2026 tariff bill are on different bases and are not presented as a change.

rr_bridge.note: Revenue requirement on a Form 1 functional basis for 2021 and 2025 (return on functional rate base at the allowed after-tax WACC, depreciation, O&M, taxes other than income, income taxes; general, intangible and A&G costs allocated to the scope by plant or O&M share; jurisdictional share applied), then the approved 2026 rate-case step. Computed in engine/lookback.py with the forward model's revenue-requirement structure. Customer service and information O&M (Form 1 accounts 907-910) includes C&LM programme costs recorded by the utility, so the operating group carries public-benefits-funded programme growth as well as distribution operations.

property_tax_attribution.method: Plant-related property tax = the property tax / net plant ratio (Form 1 page 262 property and real estate taxes charged, all departments, / Form 1 page 200 net utility plant, all departments) x the scope's functional rate-base plant (scope net plant + allocated general and intangible plant, after the jurisdictional share). Property tax is assessed on plant value, so a uniform ratio attributes it to plant in proportion to net book value; assessed values, local rates and special-franchise valuation differ by plant type and locality, so this is an attribution, not a measured split. Non-plant taxes = the scope's taxes other than income (as in the detailed bridge) - plant-related property tax (payroll, gross receipts, franchise, sales and use and other taxes).

2021.unit: share of net plant a year

2025.unit: share of net plant a year

om_normalisation.check: Not driven by pension or retiree-benefit credits: Form 1 account 926 (employee pensions and benefits) is $18.2M in 2021 and $9.7M in 2025 (positive in both years), against administrative and general costs of $218.1M and $189.7M. Reported and normalised O&M are the same.
om_normalisation.method: Normalised O&M = reported O&M (Form 1 functional basis) - non-service pension and retiree-benefit costs in administrative and general, allocated to the scope by the same O&M share as the rest of A&G and then by the jurisdictional share. The detailed bridge keeps reported O&M; the grouped view uses normalised O&M and shows the non-service change as its own reconciling line.

2021.source: Check: Form 1 account 926 is 18.2 (2021) and 9.7 (2025) $M; not credit-driven, so no normalisation is applied

2025.source: Check: Form 1 account 926 is 18.2 (2021) and 9.7 (2025) $M; not credit-driven, so no normalisation is applied

supply_side.influence: Influenced, not controlled, by the distribution utility: set by wholesale markets (PJM / NYISO / ISO-NE auctions), FERC formula rates or fuel markets; the utility affects them only through its load, procurement and the resources it connects.
